title: Chuck Taylor All-Stars
blurb: A canvas basketball shoe from 1917 that left the court and never stopped being worn.

title: Air Jordan
blurb: Michael Jordan's signature basketball shoe line, which turned sneakers into collectibles.

title: Dr. Martens
blurb: Air-cushioned work boots with yellow stitching, adopted by punks, postmen and everyone in between.

title: Moccasin
blurb: A soft deerskin shoe of Indigenous North American origin, stitched from a single piece of hide.

title: Pointe shoe
blurb: The satin ballet shoe with a stiffened box that lets a dancer stand on the tips of the toes.

title: Rancourt & Co.
about: Handmade leather shoes from Lewiston, Maine
blurb: Rancourt & Co. has handcrafted footwear in Maine since 1967: loafers, boots, boat shoes and moccasins, many built with true handsewn moccasin construction.

title: Quoddy
about: Handsewn moccasins and boots from Maine
blurb: A family business in Lewiston, Maine, making handsewn shoes, boots, moccasins and slippers by hand.

title: Fizzy Goblet
blurb: A designer footwear brand from India putting a modern twist on traditional crafts: juttis, mojaris and loafers.

title: Needledust
blurb: Handcrafted, traditional footwear, chiefly embroidered juttis for women, men and children.

title: Coral Haze
blurb: A maker of handcrafted designer juttis that aims to keep Indian craft alive as a living design language rather than a relic.

title: Mukluk
about: Soft boot of the Arctic peoples
blurb: A soft boot of caribou skin or sealskin, made and worn by the Inuit, Iñupiat and Yup'ik peoples of the Arctic. The name comes from the Yup'ik word for the bearded seal.

title: Engineer boot
about: American leather work boot from the 1930s
blurb: A lace-less leather work boot first made in the 1930s for firemen on steam locomotives, then taken up by motorcyclists and, in the 1950s, by teenagers in search of rebellion.

title: Saddle shoe
about: Shoe with a contrasting saddle-shaped panel
blurb: A low-heeled oxford with a saddle-shaped panel across the middle, usually white with black, brown or navy, and the classic school shoe of the 1940s and 1950s.

title: Boat shoe
about: Deck shoe with a siped rubber sole
blurb: A canvas or leather deck shoe whose rubber sole is cut with fine slits so it grips a wet deck. Traditionally worn without socks.

title: Huarache
blurb: A Mexican sandal of pre-Columbian origin; its name comes from warachi in the Purépecha language.
